verdict: On packets of 30 to 60 pages with Claude Haiku 5.5, holistic classification with a 10-page window is a good place to start ([SC-04](#how-long-a-packet-can-holistic-classification-handle)). It got 67% of sections exactly right, as many as splitting first and then classifying each section, for $39 of classification per 1,000 packets, against $125 for split-then-classify and $45 for page by page. With the default 20-page window, holistic and page by page both got 62%. Holistic grouped pages better (grouping score 0.88 against 0.82) but cost 2.3 times as much ($103), because its calls went over the 100,000 tokens above which Claude Haiku 5.5 charges more. Every approach did worse on long packets than on packets of 5 to 20 pages. Test it on your own packets.
